title: performance(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and add rollout guards
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production rollouts occasionally introduced subtle latency regressions under specific KV cache hit patterns and small-batch high-concurrency traffic. This PR implements an automated performance canary detector that watches latency and throughput signals during canary rollouts and blocks/rolls back traffic if regressions cross configurable thresholds. Changes include: 1) a new canary-detector service (stateless) that consumes aggregated perf metrics and runs a windowed detection algorithm with hysteresis and KV-aware baselines, 2) rollout-guard policy integration with the router that can pause traffic shifting and trigger automatic fallback, 3) telemetry additions for per-route latency P99/P95, queue time, and batch-size distribution, 4) CLI and Console UI flags to tune sensitivity and hysteresis, and 5) unit/integration tests and a perf regression test harness. Design: detector uses adaptive thresholds derived from historical baseline for the route + model variant, then applies a two-tier check: (A) immediate spike detection (fast abort if >50% P99 increase sustained for 30s) and (B) sustained degradation detection (15% P95 increase with hysteresis across 5m). The algorithm is conservative by default and can be tuned per-deployment via rollout guard policy. Backwards compatibility: default behavior for existing rollouts is unchanged until an operator opts into the guard. Migration: lightweight schema changes to metrics ingestion and a short DB migration to store per-canary baseline snapshots. Testing: included end-to-end canary scenario in perf-canary lab and synthetic traffic tests that emulate KV cache warm/cold transitions. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind "canary_auto_detect" and staged to internal oss first, then gradual opt-in for Dedicated customers. See linked Linear for rollout milestones.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Algorithm looks sound but we need to ensure the baseline snapshot volume doesn't add DB pressure during mass canaries. Suggest adding TTL + sharding for snapshots.
Aisha Kapoor: Added TTL (30d) and lightweight sharding by route hash in migration. Updated migration SQL and noted in docs.
Claire Liu: Router pause logic race condition: if a canary is paused and then another rollout for same route starts, ensure locks prevent conflicting decisions.
Aisha Kapoor: Router now acquires per-route rollout lock before applying policy decisions; added unit test simulating concurrent rollouts.
Harold Chen: Observability: include batch-size distribution and queue-time in the dashboard so SRE can triage cold-cache cases quickly.
Aisha Kapoor: Added metrics tags and Console UI panel with histogram for batch-size distribution.
SRE CI: perf-canary-regression-check flagged a false positive on small sample sizes; tuned hysteresis and min-sample thresholds and re-ran tests.
Claire Liu: Approve after CI fix and docs update.
Miguel Torres: Approved — will monitor canary runs next week in staging before GA.
Automation Bot: merging via squash after approved reviews and green CI.
changed_areas: services/canary-detector: new service implementing detection algorithm and API
router/rollout_guard: policy hooks to pause/rollback canaries
observability: new perf metrics and tags
console: UI to configure sensitivity and view canary state
perf-canary tests: e2e scenarios and synthetic traffic harness
db migrations: add canary baseline table
testing_notes: Included unit tests for algorithm edge cases, integration test that runs a synthetic canary against staging traffic, and a perf harness that validates no regression is introduced under simulated KV warm/cold conditions. Local test run: 120s synthetic scenario passed. Staging rollout: observed no false aborts in 48h of mixed-traffic experiments.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged (canary_auto_detect) disabled by default. Step 1: internal canaries (team opt-in), Step 2: opt-in for select Dedicated customers, Step 3: gradual enable via Console for higher-safety routes. Monitored metrics: P95/P99 latency, queue time, batch-size distribution. Auto rollback policy can be disabled per-route.
operational_impact: Low: detector runs statelessly and consumes aggregated metrics; minor DB add for baseline snapshots with TTL. Defaults conservative to avoid false positives. Ops playbook added to docs for manual override and forced rollback.
release_notes: Added an automated performance canary detector and rollout guards which can detect sustained latency or throughput regressions during canary rollouts and automatically pause or rollback traffic shifts. Feature is behind a feature flag and configurable per-route.
merge_outcome: Merged after approvals and CI green. Squash merge commit recorded and deployment to staging scheduled via release pipeline. Post-merge actions: DB migration scheduled during next maintenance window and Console flag gated until internal validation completes.
